rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 3-5 <U+2014> the authors collected field discharge and pressure data at the upstream end and at four hydrants of the Lucefecit on-demand network (2000-2002), calibrated a steady-state hydraulic model against observed head losses (Fig. 6), and ran ICARE and AKLA simulations (1000-2000 random hydrant configurations) to compute indexed characteristic curves, relative pressure deficits and reliability per hydrant.
rows.notes: The study contains no data or result on investment cost of on-demand networks, nor on cost being driven by guaranteeing supply at peak. What it actually shows is a hydraulic performance analysis of one on-demand network during the peak period: at the design upstream piezometric elevation (260 m) fewer than 10% of configurations are satisfied at peak discharge and several hydrants show negative relative pressure deficit and low reliability; raising Zo to 265 m improves performance but three hydrants still fail, requiring larger pipe diameters. If anything, it shows supply at peak is not fully guaranteed at the hydrants, and it does not link this to investment cost. The reliability/RPD outputs are model results from a calibrated model, with the calibration itself showing underestimation of head losses.

notes: Full text available; figures referenced but not reproduced. Study is a modelling/field case study of hydraulic performance of a single on-demand pressurized network (Lucefecit, Portugal); it does not address investment costs.
